title: BIAS, DIVERSITY, AND CHALLENGES TO FAIRNESS IN CLASSIFICATION AND AUTOMATED TEXT ANALYSIS. From libraries to AI and back

bias_targets.methodology: Qualitative analysis of historical library classification practices and the assignment of Dewey Decimal Classification (DDC) numbers to works by Black authors.

Analyzing differential density and hierarchical granularity in the Dewey Decimal Classification (DDC) system, specifically comparing the detailed sub-categories for Christianity versus the coarse grouping of other religions.

Qualitative evaluation of GPT-2 text generation using a prompt about a female AI scientist to observe stereotypical keyword associations (e.g., knitting/textiles), alongside a review of sexist search engine autocomplete suggestions.
Tracing the historical evolution and problematic contextual placement of LGBTQ+ categories within the Dewey Decimal Classification (DDC) system over time.
Reviewing normative language and terminology changes in the Library of Congress Subject Headings (LCSH), specifically the transition from 'illegal aliens' to 'noncitizen'.
